question: Why did all three original candidate runs appear slower, and does the correlation survive fixed CPU affinity?

perf_control.artifact: A second attempt to preserve the output was blocked by content-exclusion policy and was not retried.

conclusions: Fixed affinity substantially narrows direct-replay spread: CPU0 is 18.77-24.52 seconds and CPU16 18.92-27.67, versus 17.95-47.39 unpinned.
The original candidate-only slowdown does not survive either fixed-CPU control. Candidate wins all five genuine pairs on both CPUs.
CPU16 is especially stable: baseline/candidate medians are 56.78/45.94 seconds and Z3 medians 26.14/25.30.

Original candidate runs had 8,304-12,716 involuntary context switches versus 230-254 for baseline. This, affinity sensitivity, and paired reversal support an environmental scheduler/CPU-execution effect, but do not identify its exact hardware mechanism.
limitations: Affinity constrains placement but does not reserve a CPU from other host workloads.
No cycles/instructions counters were available, so frequency, SMT-sibling contention, and other hardware-level causes remain unresolved.
No production source change was made.
